sequences.mechanism: Presynaptic calcium-dependent ACh release → muscle end-plate potential and action potential → T-membrane voltage sensing → SR calcium release → regulated ATP-dependent cross-bridge cycling → calcium reuptake

steps.signal: presynaptic action potential and extracellular calcium entry
steps.representation: explained; terminal calcium channels and fusion machinery not individually modeled

steps.signal: ACh diffusion across cleft and binding to nicotinic receptors

steps.effect: propagated electrical signal, not movement of ACh through the cell

steps.signal: T-membrane CaV1.1 voltage sensing coupled to SR RyR1 activation
steps.representation: coupling proteins named in text only; precise molecular contact arrangement not reconstructed

steps.signal: calcium binds troponin C; tropomyosin inhibition is reduced

steps.destination: filament sliding and tension under appropriate load
steps.effect: repeated attachment, force generation, ATP-dependent detachment and recovery
steps.representation: static head examples; no motion, nucleotide states or force kinetics

steps.signal: cessation of nerve drive; cleft ACh breakdown
steps.effect: no continuing muscle excitation in this normal teaching sequence
reduces thin-filament activation; does not specify a return-to-reference length

schematic_limitations: Static native teaching views; no molecular particles, kinetics, voltage traces or channel geometry.
No arrow or teaching text connects T lumen with SR lumen.
Terminal covering and membranes have teaching openings and exaggerated separation.
Presynaptic extracellular calcium entry and intracellular muscle SR calcium release occur in separate cells and must never share a particle route.
The end-plate potential is a local graded signal; the propagated muscle action potential is a distinct event.
Physical skeletal coupling is described at pathway level; exact atomic binding and channel-gating geometry are not claimed.
Load is unspecified; activation does not establish shortening, force magnitude or a return-to-reference displacement.
sequences.implementation: Static exact-name camera views and native lesson text with explicit View-menu instructions. Lesson does not apply camera visibility; no particles, solver, channel animation or timing.

sequences.mechanism: Optional static reference and increased-overlap coordinate examples, with no physiological resting-state designation
sequences.implementation: sarcomere_states.py intervals()/comparison(); the initial reference exists in recovered source, increased-overlap geometry is not constructed. H-zone-null boundary is a scalar test only.
schematic_limitations: Numbers are enlarged source coordinates, not measured anatomy.
No force percentage, no linear force equation and no active tension inferred from shortening.
Bare-zone constant is a separate illustrative parameter; avoid making it follow H-zone boundaries.
No native animation or second-state geometry is claimed implemented by this specialist.
Each half-I interval is reported within one Z-to-Z sarcomere; the complete I band straddles a Z disc between adjacent sarcomeres.
Reference/increased_overlap are mechanism-example names, never Pre refine/Post refine labels.
Do not map these source units onto the frog-fiber experimental micrometre values or a human optimal length.
sequences.bare_zone_parameter_origin: Matches construction deferred_stages.py head omission M±0.004, width 0.008 source units; purely illustrative, not biological calibration.

sequences.mechanism: Represented arterial supply -> connected exchange sample -> venous collection in supporting tissue
schematic_limitations: Three capillary paths and two cross-link levels are a teaching sample.
Trunk endpoint cuts represent continuation beyond the sampled field.
Saved lumen continuity and cell clearance await heavy validation; path annotations alone do not prove them.
No numerical exchange, pressure, saturation or velocity simulation.
sequences.implementation: Static source-authored route; saved lumen continuity remains deferred.

sequences.mechanism: Parallel muscle elongation deforms central intrafusal sensory region; polar contraction controls spindle tension

steps.relation: central Ia sensory ending signals muscle length and its rate of change; contractile poles regulate central sensory-region tension

schematic_limitations: No length-discharge calibration, gamma axon geometry, secondary endings, alpha-gamma coordination simulation or reflex circuit.
Intrafusal polar action is explained without claiming contribution to represented whole-muscle force.
Bag/chain nuclear groups remain surrounded by opened cell walls, not revealed by removing all context.
sequences.implementation: Static capsule/intrafusal/Ia geometry and lesson explanation; no length sensor simulation.

scale_note: SCHEMATIC: variable enlargement; positions, thicknesses and relative lengths are not microscopic measurements.

delivery_variant_policy.pre_refine: The new source-improved model after its authorized build and before microrefine.
delivery_variant_policy.post_refine: A separately processed output; never obtained by renaming the reference/increased-overlap examples.
delivery_variant_policy.display: Exactly one processing variant visible at a time; static geometric examples do not change variant provenance.

source_evidence.title: UTHealth Neuroscience Online, Chapter 5: Mechanisms of Neurotransmitter Release
source_evidence.decision_support_and_limits: Presynaptic depolarization admits extracellular calcium; calcium-dependent vesicle release. No quantal counts or times are adopted.

source_evidence.title: UTHealth Neuroscience Online, Chapter 4: Synaptic Transmission at the Skeletal Neuromuscular Junction
source_evidence.decision_support_and_limits: Local end-plate depolarization versus propagated muscle action potential; threshold distinction, ligand-gated receptor and transmitter termination.

source_evidence.title: University of Leeds, Muscle: Neuromuscular Junction
source_evidence.decision_support_and_limits: Vesicular ACh, cleft diffusion and cleft-basal-lamina-associated acetylcholinesterase. Motor-end-plate terminology is resolved using explicit postsynaptic source, not one ambiguous introductory sentence.

source_evidence.title: University of Leeds, Muscle Stimulation
source_evidence.decision_support_and_limits: Sarcolemmal T invagination at A–I junction, triad, SR release and reuptake. No molecular dimensions or timing adopted.

source_evidence.title: Dulhunty and Casarotto (2026), The nuts and bolts of excitation–contraction coupling in skeletal muscle
source_evidence.inspected_scope: Opened full page: Introduction and structural framework; lines 68–128
source_evidence.decision_support_and_limits: Skeletal physical coupling from CaV1.1-associated voltage sensing to SR RyR1; current review explicitly distinguishes established pathway from unresolved precise molecular interactions. No exact atomic link or gating conformation is modeled.

source_evidence.title: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 10.3 Muscle Fiber Contraction and Relaxation
source_evidence.inspected_scope: Opened section text: sliding filament model, ATP and muscle contraction, relaxation
source_evidence.decision_support_and_limits: Troponin/tropomyosin regulation; ATP-dependent head detachment and recovery. Use only these qualitative relationships, not page-specific stroke sizes, metabolic percentages or its simplified SR-channel wording.

source_evidence.title: Smith et al. (2013), ATP Consumption by Sarcoplasmic Reticulum Ca2+ Pumps Accounts for 40-50% of Resting Metabolic Rate in Mouse Fast and Slow Twitch Skeletal Muscle
source_evidence.inspected_scope: Opened full paper: Introduction and Discussion
source_evidence.decision_support_and_limits: ATP-consuming SERCA transport, distinct from myosin ATPase. Mouse experimental metabolic percentages are not transferred into this schematic.

source_evidence.title: University of Leeds, Muscle Ultrastructure
source_evidence.decision_support_and_limits: Sarcomere bands, anchors and sliding-filament structural relationships; no mapping from source coordinates to biological length.

source_evidence.title: Histology Guide, EM 339 Neuromuscular Junction
source_evidence.inspected_scope: Opened textual Skeletal Muscle Cell section; lines 162–167
source_evidence.decision_support_and_limits: A-band overlap, H-band thick-only and I-band thin-only identity. Do not adopt this page’s simplified ACh/Ca-channel sentence as the NMJ ionic mechanism.

source_evidence.title: Luther (2026), Structure of the Myosin Thick Filaments in Muscle
source_evidence.decision_support_and_limits: Antiparallel thick-filament central bare organization distinguished from absence-of-thin H zone. Does not supply a measured bare width for this skeletal schematic.

source_evidence.title: Gordon, Huxley and Julian (1966), The variation in isometric tension with sarcomere length in vertebrate muscle fibres
source_evidence.decision_support_and_limits: Frog-fiber isometric length–tension plateau and short-length decline support rejecting a universal linear overlap-to-force relation. Experimental dimensions are not schematic calibration.

source_evidence.title: University of Leeds, Muscle: Skeletal Muscle Connective Tissue
source_evidence.decision_support_and_limits: Connective tissue and neurovascular location. Source path claims are not saved-lumen evidence.

source_evidence.title: UTHealth Neuroscience Online, Section 2 Chapter 2: Somatosensory Systems
source_evidence.decision_support_and_limits: Parallel intrafusal context, central primary sensory ending, polar gamma endplates, length/rate sensing. No discharge or force calibration.
